memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, system interventions, and field evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the system.
Cross-check whether field tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether the evidence to be collected aligns with the design and operational decisions to be changed.
Finally verify that the user problem, system intervention, field evaluation, and expected contribution form one coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions do not connect to system functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if field tasks fail to generate representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practical utility of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Before submission, conduct a sequential walkthrough with field liaisons of installation failures, operational interruptions, and recovery scenarios.
Verify in one sentence how each proposed contribution could actually alter specific design or operational decisions.
The user must distinguish unconfirmed field partners and equipment from finalized ones so remaining execution risks can be assessed.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains: participant-compensation policy versus pre-submission validation of HCI proposals and field execution. No claim in either frame has a sufficiently corresponding claim in the other, so all substantive information remains independently useful and one-sided.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines coherence and alignment checks for HCI proposals, reviewer-facing rationales, operational-failure walkthroughs, contribution-to-decision tests, and disclosure of unresolved field resources.
reports.reference_only: The reference frames compensation around total participant burden, equitable rates, flexible payment planning, iterative-study demands, early termination, and a noted tendency to omit between-session preparation.
